topics: security: SOC 2, VPC, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, i'm the ae on this account. quick intro?
[00:07] Samir Patel: yeah hi all, samir here, cto at aurora analytics. emily and jordan are on the call too.
[00:12] Emily Park: hi, emily, head of ml.
[00:14] Jordan Lee: jordan, eng manager.
[00:16] Liam Ortiz: and i'm liam, solutions engineer at redwood, i'll nerd out on performance stuff.
[00:20] Maya Chen: awesome. high level — we're here to understand your inference workloads and see whether hosted, dedicated, or a private deployment makes sense. also quickstart — free credits and how fast you can get first token.
[00:33] Samir Patel: perfect. high level, we run inference for two products — real-time recommendations (p99 latency target ~120ms) and batch enrichment (hundreds of thousands of requests nightly). data residency in us-west is preferred, and we have strict audit requirements.
[00:48] Liam Ortiz: okay that helps. for real-time 120ms p99 is pretty tight depending on model size and sequence length — are you using smaller transformer variants or larger ones today?
[00:56] Emily Park: we use a 7B open model for most requests, occasionally 13B for higher-quality results. we're experimenting with quantization but haven't committed.
[01:05] Maya Chen: great, that aligns with a lot of customers. hosted can get you started fastest — free credits, API keys, time-to-first-token in minutes. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable latency/throughput, and Private gives full VPC/on-prem for regulated data.
[01:22] Jordan Lee: curious on the quickstart — how long to get a team member running a simple generate call?
[01:26] Maya Chen: you can sign up and hit the sandbox in under 10 minutes. with our SDK/REST example you'll have a token, a sample prompt, and streaming response in like 5-10 minutes. we also provide a quickstart repo.
[01:36] Emily Park: and free credits? how much?
[01:38] Maya Chen: for trials we typically provide $500 of credits for PLG trials, enough to run some benchmarks. if you want dedicated sizing or a pilot we add reserved trial capacity too.
[01:47] Samir Patel: ok, that's helpful. security — we need SOC 2, SSO, audit logs, and customer-managed keys.
[01:54] Liam Ortiz: yep, we support SOC 2 reports, SAML SSO / SSO integrations, RBAC in the console, and KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments. hosted customers can use our key management options or bring-your-own-key in some plans. audit logs are available in the console and via APIs.
[02:10] Samir Patel: when you say bring-your-own-key for hosted, is that an envelope encryption with our KMS?
[02:15] Liam Ortiz: it's envelope style — we integrate with major cloud KMS providers. for the strictest controls, Private gives full KMS control in your VPC. we can share the security pack after this call.
[02:25] Jordan Lee: on latency/cost, you mentioned batching and KV caching — can you explain how those reduce cost without breaking p99?
[02:31] Liam Ortiz: sure. KV/prefix caching keeps recent context in fast memory and avoids re-computation for stateless prefix tokens; continuous batching groups requests at the runtime level. we tune batching window to meet latency SLOs so throughput increases but p99 stays within your target. quantization can further reduce GPU footprint, with some quality tradeoff.
[02:52] Emily Park: do you have examples where customers moved from hosted to dedicated? how big a jump is that operationally?
[02:58] Maya Chen: yes — most start hosted (fastest time to value), run benchmarks, then move to Dedicated when they need predictable cost and higher throughput. operationally it's a config and capacity reservation — we help with the migration and model pinning. Private is larger step — network configs and customer-managed infra.
[03:15] Samir Patel: we also need to run a small benchmark — compare latency/cost vs our current infra. can redwood run the benchmark or provide a config?
[03:23] Liam Ortiz: we can provide a benchmark harness and recommended prompt sets; we can also run a short benchmark on a Dedicated trial cluster if you want — that would require some input like request distribution and sample prompts.
[03:33] Maya Chen: + we'll include the pricing worksheet so you can model reserved vs on-demand.
[03:38] Jordan Lee: on private options — we're not air-gapped but want VPC peering and strict egress rules. is that supported?
[03:44] Liam Ortiz: yes, Private supports VPC peering and on-prem packages; you can restrict egress and we've got audit hooks.
[03:49] Emily Park: any notable quirks in the quickstart? for example, do we need internal approvals for network access?
[03:54] Maya Chen: typically for hosted quickstart you don't — it's just API keys. for Dedicated/Private you'll coordinate with your infra/security teams for network and IAM.
[04:03] Samir Patel: we have an internal procurement timeline — likely pilot in 3-4 weeks, production in 2-3 months if benchmarks look good.
[04:10] Maya Chen: that timeline sounds reasonable. for pilot success criteria, what metrics matter? latency p99, cost per request, quality (precision of recs?) and reliability.
[04:20] Emily Park: yes — p99 < 120ms for RT path, 95% generation quality on our eval set, and cost under $X/token (we'll share numbers).
[04:30] Liam Ortiz: noted. i'll put together a config for running these tests.
[04:34] Maya Chen: any competitors you're also evaluating?
[04:36] Samir Patel: mainly openai and anthropic for hosted, and we're talking to a couple of infra vendors for dedicated.
[04:42] Maya Chen: understood. we'll include differentiation notes — e.g., model routing, KV cache, transparent latency/cost dashboards.
[04:49] Jordan Lee: question on model pinning — if we pin a model version, do rollouts support canary traffic?
[04:54] Liam Ortiz: yes, rollouts support canary and A/B style policies with automatic fallback to previous model if errors spike.
[05:01] Emily Park: about data retention: hosted default retention is 30 days? can that be shortened?
[05:06] Maya Chen: by default logs are retained per plan, but we can configure retention windows; for strict customers we recommend Private where you control retention.
[05:13] Samir Patel: what's the SLA for Dedicated?
[05:16] Maya Chen: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets — details in the enterprise agreement; we'll include the SLA doc.
[05:23] Jordan Lee: okay, let's talk concrete next steps.
[05:26] Maya Chen: agreed. we'll send: pricing worksheet, security pack (SOC 2, encryption, SSO docs), benchmark harness, and invite for tech deep-dive on 2026-10-01.
[05:37] Samir Patel: sounds good. Emily, anything else?
[05:39] Emily Park: no, that's everything, thanks.
[05:41] Maya Chen: cool — recap: maya sends docs + pricing, liam prepares benchmark config, emily shares targets. schedule deep-dive.
[05:50] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone.
[05:51] Maya Chen: thanks, bye.
[48:30] (call end)
